I’d love to hear from you. vudiphothisukart@gmail.com The artist behind the work Art, experienced. To me, art is more than something to look at. It's something to experience — a conversation starter, a memory holder, and a way to bring life into a space. I create mixed-media paintings that bring together sculptural texture, layered color, and organic forms. Through each collection, I explore the relationship between nature, form, and the world around us. I want my work to invite people to pause, look closer, and discover something new each time. title: Mother Nature | Forest & Flowers | Vudi Phothisuk Art
description: A hidden goddess emerges from the forest, her profile formed by the leaves, vines, and flowers that surround her. Beside her, a pale river winds between densely textured mountains, drawing the eye into the landscape. Sculpted foliage and metallic highlights reveal a presence that might initially go unnoticed.

Beside her, a pale river winds between densely textured mountains, drawing the eye into the landscape. Sculpted foliage and metallic highlights reveal a presence that might initially go unnoticed. Mother Nature considers the contradictions in our relationship with the natural world: we depend on its generosity, yet often mistake that dependence for ownership. The painting asks us to look more closely, and to recognize the difference between appreciating nature and believing we control it. Blooming Desire explores the excitement of finding someone who makes the ordinary feel unfamiliar again, opening a world of experiences to discover together. Each blossom has its own irregular shape, bringing the painting’s idea of imperfect connection into physical form. The swirling textures echo the exchange of thoughts, feelings, and possibilities that accompanies a new relationship. There is pleasure in the uncertainty of what might emerge, and in making the attempt together. text: Back to collection 05 / 10 — Forest & Flowers A Forest Forgotten 24 × 36 in. $5,000 Mixed-media acrylic with organic plaster on canvas Full composition Enlarge artwork Tap the photograph to enlarge Mixed-media acrylic with organic plaster on canvas About the painting A towering tree trunk fills the center of A Forest Forgotten, its deeply worked surface rising beyond the canvas. Around it, sculpted leaves and pale flowers frame glimpses of green forest beneath a sky of pink, gold, and blue. The close viewpoint gives the tree a commanding presence while allowing the surrounding landscape to remain partly concealed. Inspired by the conservation work of Paul Rosolie and Junglekeepers , the painting reflects on the beauty and vulnerability of rainforests, and on the distance between recognizing their value and acting to protect them. It brings that concern into a tangible encounter with bark, foliage, color, and scale. A Forest Forgotten — Art for Conservation 20% of profits from this original artwork and its Studio Prints will be donated to Junglekeepers in support of rainforest conservation. Closer look At the Base of the Trunk The close view puts the small forms of the undergrowth beside the trunk’s long grooves. Green gathers between dark ridges, and the scale of the tree becomes clearer through the forms growing around it. Undergrowth at the Trunk The Forest Behind the Bark From the side, the trunk’s raised surface stands forward while fragments of pale sky and green forest remain visible around it. The view holds both the tree and its surroundings in sight, an intimate perspective on the rainforest at the center of the work. text: Back to collection 09 / 10 — Forest & Flowers 75 Leaves 24 × 36 in. Mixed-media acrylic with organic plaster on canvas Full composition Enlarge artwork Tap the photograph to enlarge Mixed-media acrylic with organic plaster on canvas About the painting A blue-and-gold current, representing the Elbe River, winds through layered passages of green, pink, and metallic texture. 75 Leaves pays tribute to WWII pilot Wallace N. “Wally” King. Each of its 75 sculpted leaves represents one of the 75 combat missions he flew. Among the foliage, a single golden-bronze leaf stands apart: a tribute to King’s life and a reminder that humanity and hope can endure amid war. The flowing composition brings these meanings into an organic landscape, holding courage and sacrifice alongside the beauty of life.
